yamami.phenology

Vegetation phenology analysis module for YAMAMI.

This module provides functions for computing greenness ratio (GR) time series and extracting phenological dates using double-sigmoid curve fitting.

The main functions are: - gr(): Compute greenness ratio from RGB images - fit_double_sigmoid(): Fit double-sigmoid curve to time series - phenology(): Extract phenological dates (green-up, green-max, green-down)

Example usage:
>>> from yamami.phenology import gr, phenology
>>> images, timeseries = gr(profile_df, aoi_mask)
>>> pheno_dates = phenology(timeseries)
yamami.phenology.gr(profile, aoi_mask, daily_max=True, output_dir=None)[source]

Compute greenness ratio time series from image profile.

Calculates GR = G / (R + G + B) for each pixel within the AOI mask, optionally aggregating to daily maximum values.

Parameters:

  • profile (DataFrame) – DataFrame with ‘filepath’ and ‘timestamp’ columns.

  • aoi_mask (ndarray) – Boolean mask array defining the area of interest. Pixels with True are included in the analysis.

  • daily_max (bool) – If True, aggregate multiple observations per day to daily maximum value. Default is True.

  • output_dir (str | None) – Optional directory to save intermediate GR images.

Returns:

  • daily_images: Dict mapping date strings to GR image arrays

  • timeseries: DataFrame with date, doy, and mean_gr columns

Return type:

Tuple of (daily_images, timeseries) where

Raises:

ValueError – If profile is empty or missing required columns.

yamami.phenology.fit_double_sigmoid(time, values, max_iter=5000)[source]

Fit double-sigmoid curve to greenness time series.

Uses scipy.optimize.curve_fit with bounds to fit the double-sigmoid model to observed GR values.

Parameters:

  • time (ndarray) – Time values (typically day of year), shape (N,).

  • values (ndarray) – GR values corresponding to time points, shape (N,).

  • max_iter (int) – Maximum iterations for curve fitting. Default is 5000.

Returns:

  • ‘params’: Fitted parameters (base, amp1, k1, t1, amp2, k2, t2)

  • ’t1’ (gup_doy): Green-up date (inflection of rising sigmoid)

  • ’t2’ (gdown_doy): Green-down date (inflection of falling sigmoid)

  • ’gmax_doy’: Date of maximum fitted value

  • ’gmax_value’: Maximum fitted value

  • ’fit_rmse’: Root mean square error of fit

  • ’fit_status’: ‘success’ or ‘failed’

Return type:

Dictionary containing

yamami.phenology.phenology(gr_data, model='double_sigmoid', output_dir=None)[source]

Extract phenology dates from GR time series.

Fits a phenological model to the GR time series and extracts key dates: - gup_doy: Green-up date (inflection point of rising phase) - gdown_doy: Green-down date (inflection point of falling phase) - gmax_doy: Date of maximum greenness

Parameters:

  • gr_data (dict | DataFrame) – Either a DataFrame with ‘doy’ and ‘mean_gr’ columns, or a dict of date-indexed GR images from gr() function.

  • model (str) – Phenological model to use. Currently only ‘double_sigmoid’ is supported. Default is ‘double_sigmoid’.

  • output_dir (str | None) – Optional directory to save fitted curve data.

Returns:

  • row, col: Pixel coordinates (if pixel-level fitting)

  • gup_doy: Green-up day of year

  • gdown_doy: Green-down day of year

  • gmax_doy: Day of maximum greenness

  • gmax_value: Maximum greenness value

  • fit_rmse: Root mean square error of fit

  • fit_status: ‘success’ or ‘failed’

Return type:

DataFrame with columns

Raises:

ValueError – If model is not recognized or gr_data format is invalid.
